[2023:RJ-JD:43889] HIGH COURT OF JUDICATURE FOR RAJASTHAN AT JODHPUR S.B.
Criminal Miscellaneous Bail Application No. 15209/2023 Nema Ram S/o Kalu Ram, Aged About 34 Years, R/o Kosana, Police Station Peepar City, Dist. Jodhpur.

entities.text: HIGH COURT OF JUDICATURE FOR RAJASTHAN AT JODHPUR
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
(At Present Lodged At Balotra Jail)
----Applicant Versus 1. State Of Rajasthan, Through Pp 2. L W/o Hadman Ram, R/o Richoli, Police Station Pachpadra, Dist. Balotra, Rajasthan.

----Respondents For Applicant (s) : Mr. Om Prakash Joshi with Mr. Karan Joshi For Respondent(s)
: Mr. Mukhtiyar Khan, Public Prosecutor Mr. M.M. Dhera, for the complainant JUSTICE DINESH MEHTA Order 15/12/2023 1.

This application for bail has been filed by the applicant under section 439 of the Code of Criminal Procedure in connection with FIR No.311/2023, Police Station - Pachpadra, District - Balotra for the offences under Section 366, 376 (2)(N) of Indian Penal Code, 1860.
2. Mr. Joshi, learned counsel for the applicant argued that a false case has been lodged by the prosecutrix.

3. Learned counsel for the applicant invited Court's attention towards the order dated 05.10.2023,
passed by a Coordinate Bench of this Court and submitted that the applicant and the prosecutrix had been living in live-in relationship for which, they [2023:RJ-JD:43889] (2 of 3)
] have sought order of protection from this Court by way of filing a petition being S.B. Criminal Writ Petition No.1677/2023 and having an agreement dated 26.09.2023.

4. Learned counsel submitted that the physical relationship between the applicant and prosecutrix was that of consent and the FIR has been lodged out of vengeance, when the relationship between the applicant and the prosecutrix became sour.
5. Learned Public Prosecutor and Mr. Dhera, for the complainant vehemently opposed the bail application.

6. Heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the material available on record.

entities.text: Nema Ram vs State Of Rajasthan (2023:Rj-Jd:43889)
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Having regard to the facts and circumstances of the case and considering the agreement dated 26.09.2023 and the order dated 05.10.2023, this Court is of the prima-facie view that the relationship between the applicant and the prosecutrix was that of consent, which is further evident from the fact that the prosecutrix has travelled with the present applicant to Pachpadra, and various other places.
8. Consequently, the bail application filed under section 439 of the Code of Criminal Procedure is allowed.

The applicant Nema Ram S/o Kalu Ram arrested in connection with FIR No.311/2023,
Police Station - Pachpadra, District - Balotra shall be released on bail on his furnishing personal bond in the sum of Rs.50,000/- and two sureties of Rs.25,000/- each to the satisfaction of the trial Court.
9. Applicant shall be required to appear before that Court on all dates of hearing and as and when called upon to do so.

[2023:RJ-JD:43889] (3 of 3) [CRLMB-15209/2023]
10. Needless to mention that the above observations made by this Court are on the basis of material so far produced before the Court.

These are only prima-facie observations and the same shall however, not come in the way of the trial Court to take independent view of the matter, based on ocular and oral evidence, while finally deciding the case.

(DINESH MEHTA),J 82-himanshu/-
